title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 53 (Prohibition on Issue of Shares at a Discount)

content.overview: Section 53 generally prohibits issuing shares at a discount and declares a discounted issue void, subject to two statutory routes: sweat equity under section 54 and a qualifying creditor debt-conversion issue under subsection (2A). Non-compliance attracts a penalty capped at the lesser of the amount raised through the discounted issue or ₹5,00,000, and the company must refund monies received with 12% annual interest from the issue date.

content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 53 (Prohibition on issue of shares at discount). Except as provided in section 54, a company must not issue shares at a discount, and a share issued at a discount is void. Subsection (2A) creates a separate exception for shares issued at a discount to creditors when debt is converted into shares under a statutory resolution plan or debt restructuring scheme in accordance with applicable RBI guidelines, directions or regulations. Under subsection (3), the company and every officer in default are liable to a penalty that may extend to the lesser of the amount raised through the discounted issue or ₹5,00,000. The company must also refund all monies received with interest at 12% per annum from the date of issue to the persons to whom the shares were issued. Do not confuse the sweat-equity route under section 54 with the creditor-conversion exception under subsection (2A).

sections.heading: General prohibition and voidness
sections.body: Except as provided in section 54, a company must not issue shares at a discount. A share issued at a discount is void.

sections.heading: Sweat equity exception
sections.body: Section 54 provides a separate, regulated route for sweat equity shares subject to its eligibility, resolution and prescribed conditions.

sections.heading: Creditor debt-conversion exception
sections.body: Subsection (2A) permits discounted shares to creditors when debt is converted into shares under a statutory resolution plan or debt restructuring scheme in accordance with applicable RBI guidelines, directions or regulations.

sections.heading: Penalty and refund
sections.body: The company and every officer in default are liable to a penalty up to the lesser of the amount raised through the discounted issue or ₹5,00,000. The company must refund all monies received with 12% annual interest from the issue date.

examples.title: Discounted issue void
examples.body: A company issues ₹10 face-value shares at ₹8. The issue is void under s. 53; consideration must be returned with interest.

examples.title: Sweat equity exception
examples.body: Shares issued as sweat equity under s. 54 in accordance with that section fall outside the s. 53 prohibition.

hypotheticals.question: A company issues shares at a discount outside a statutory exception. What consequences follow?
hypotheticals.analysis: The shares are void. The company and every officer in default may face a penalty capped at the lesser of the amount raised through the discounted issue or ₹5,00,000, and the company must refund monies received with 12% annual interest from the issue date.

hypotheticals.question: A creditor receives shares at a discount under a qualifying debt restructuring scheme. What must be checked?
hypotheticals.analysis: Verify that the debt conversion falls under a statutory resolution plan or debt restructuring scheme and complies with the applicable RBI guidelines, directions or regulations for subsection (2A).

misconceptions.trap: Treating all discounted issues as void without checking the statutory exceptions.
misconceptions.correction: Check section 54 sweat equity and subsection (2A) qualifying creditor debt conversion.

misconceptions.trap: Applying the former fine/imprisonment wording as current subsection (3).
misconceptions.correction: Current subsection (3) provides a penalty capped at the lesser of amount raised or ₹5,00,000, plus refund with 12% annual interest.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming the refund and penalty are alternatives.
misconceptions.correction: The company is liable to refund the monies with interest, in addition to the statutory penalty.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the current subsection (3) penalty?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: A penalty up to the lesser of the amount raised through the discounted issue or ₹5,00,000 for the company and every officer in default; the company must also refund monies with 12% annual interest from issue date.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What are the statutory routes that can permit discounted shares?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Sweat equity under section 54 and qualifying creditor debt conversion under subsection (2A), each subject to its own conditions.
